skillsSummary: To install computer software. It involves installing computer software, testing computer software functionality and performing software maintenance.

criteria: 1.1 Computer software identified as per user need.
1.2 Computer software selected as per workplace procedure.
1.3 Local user accounts are created as per the workplace procedures
1.4 Data Backup performed as per work procedure.
1.5 Computer Software is installed as per software installation manual.
1.6 Computer Software is configured as per software installation manual.
2.1 Software testing is performed as per user manual.
2.2 Corrective measures are performed as per user requirements.
2.3 Computer software functionality is confirmed as per workplace procedures
3.1 Software maintenance schedule is adopted as per workplace procedure.
3.2 Software functionality is monitored as per workplace procedure.
3.3 Software upgrade is conducted as per installation guide.
3.4 Software update is conducted as per the workplace procedures.
3.5 Safety procedures are observed as per workplace procedures.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Define computer software and its purpose.  b. Classify computer software into major categories.  c. Differentiate between various types of computer software.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;  - Deliver a presentation explaining the definition and purpose of computer software.  - Facilitate an interactive activity to classify different software examples.  - Lead a group discussion on the characteristics and uses of different software types.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Participate in the presentation by asking questions and clarifying understanding.  - Engage in the interactive classification activity and justify their choices.  - Contribute to the group discussion by sharing examples and differentiating software types.  Assignment: Research and list five examples of system software and five examples of application software, explaining their primary functions.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Sommerville (2015) Ch.1 – used to explain software categories & OS roles  Resources;   - Textbooks on computer fundamentals  - PowerPoint presentations on software concepts  - Whiteboard and markers  - Computers (1:1 ratio)  - Projector
assessments: Skills   - Q&A during presentation  Knowledge   - Observation of classification activity  - Peer feedback during group discussion  - Review of assignment submissions

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify methods for collecting user needs for software.  b. Apply chosen methods to gather specific user requirements.  c. Present findings from user needs collection.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Conduct a mini-lecture on various techniques for collecting user needs (e.g., surveys, interviews).  - Organize a role-playing exercise where trainees practice interviewing 'users'.  - Guide trainees in structuring and presenting their collected user requirements.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Observe the mini-lecture and discuss different techniques for collecting user needs.  - Participate in the role-playing exercise, practicing interview techniques.  - Prepare and present the simulated user requirements to the class.  Assignment: Draft a questionnaire to gather user needs for a specific type of software application.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Pressman & Maxim (2019) Ch.5 – guides requirements elicitation & documentation  Resources;   - Case studies on user requirement gathering  - Handouts on interview/survey techniques  - Whiteboard and markers  - Computers (1:1 ratio)
assessments: Skills   - Participation in role-play  - Evaluation of presentation skills  Knowledge  - Review of draft questionnaire

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Analyze key factors influencing computer software selection.  b. Evaluate software selection criteria based on user needs.  c. Justify software choices considering various technical and non-technical aspects.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Lead a brainstorming session to identify potential factors in software selection.  - Provide a scenario-based activity where trainees evaluate software options against criteria.  - Facilitate a debate on the importance of different software selection factors.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Engage in the brainstorming session, contributing ideas on software selection factors.  - Work in groups on the scenario-based activity, evaluating software based on given criteria.  - Participate in the debate, defending their justifications for software choices.  Assignment: Prepare a comparative analysis of two software solutions for a given business problem.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Sommerville (2015) Ch.1 – used to explain software categories & OS roles  Resources;   - Software product specification sheets  - Industry best practices documents  - Internet access for research  - Computers (1:1 ratio)
assessments: Skills   - Group activity performance  -Argumentation in debate  Knowledge   - Assessment of comparative analysis report

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Describe various methods for acquiring computer software.  b. Compare the advantages and disadvantages of different acquisition methods.  c. Select the most appropriate software acquisition method for specific scenarios.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Explain different software acquisition methods (e.g., purchase, open source, cloud-based).  - Organize a problem-solving task where groups analyze scenarios and compare acquisition methods.  - Guide a class discussion to consolidate understanding and decision-making processes.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Listen to the explanation and ask clarifying questions about acquisition methods.  - Collaborate in groups on the problem-solving task, comparing and contrasting methods.  - Participate in the class discussion, justifying their selected acquisition methods.  Assignment: Outline the acquisition process for a new operating system for a small business, detailing the chosen method.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Gattiker (2005) Ch.4 – covers software licensing, compliance, and procurement ethics  Resources;   - Articles on software licensing and procurement  - Case studies on software implementation projects
assessments: Skills   - Group problem-solving outcomes  - Quality of discussion contributions  Knowledge   - Review of outlined acquisition process

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain the purpose and importance of local user accounts.  b. Distinguish between different types of local user accounts.  c. Recognize the roles and permissions associated with various account types.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;  - Conduct a lecture on the fundamental concepts of local user accounts and security.  - Present visual examples and demonstrations of different user account types on an operating system.  - Facilitate a Q&A session to clarify roles and permission differences.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Actively listen to the lecture, taking notes and asking questions about user accounts.  - Observe the demonstrations and identify the visual distinctions between account types.  - Participate in the Q&A, articulating their understanding of account roles and permissions.  Assignment: Research and document the default permissions for 'Standard User' and 'Administrator' accounts in a common operating system.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Pressman & Maxim (2019) Ch.5 – guides requirements elicitation & documentation  Resources;   - Operating system documentation  - Security best practices guides  - Computer with projected display  - Whiteboard and markers
assessments: Skills   - Engagement in Q&A  - Verbal comprehension checks  Knowledge     - Accuracy of documented research

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Prepare the necessary information and settings for creating a user account.  b. Perform the steps to create a local user account on an operating system.  c. Verify the successful creation and initial functionality of the new account.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Demonstrate the step-by-step process of creating various local user accounts.  - Supervise trainees as they practice creating different types of user accounts.  - Provide immediate feedback and troubleshoot common issues during the practice session.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Observe the demonstration attentively, noting each step in the account creation process.  - Practice creating local user accounts, following the demonstrated steps.  - Test the newly created accounts and verify their functionality, asking for clarification when needed.  Assignment: Create a new 'Guest' account with specific temporary permissions on a practice machine and document the process.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Iheagwara & Blyth (2003) – best practices in deployment planning & backup strategies  Resources;   - Practice computers (1:1 ratio) with administrative access  - Operating system user management guides  - Projector for demonstration
assessments: Skills   - Observation of practical skill during account creation  - Verification of account functionality  Knowledge   - Review of documented creation process

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify various configuration settings available for local user accounts.  b. Apply specific configurations to modify user account properties.  c. Test the applied configurations to ensure they meet specified requirements.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Explain and demonstrate how to modify various user account settings (e.g., password policies, group memberships).  - Present scenarios requiring specific account configurations for trainees to implement.  - Lead a peer review session where trainees verify each other's configurations and offer suggestions.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Observe the demonstration of account configuration and take notes on different settings.  - Work through the presented scenarios, applying the required account configurations.  - Participate in the peer review, testing configurations and providing constructive feedback.  Assignment: Configure a 'Standard User' account with restricted access to specific applications and folders on a practice machine.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Pressman & Maxim (2019) Ch.5 – guides requirements elicitation & documentation  Resources;   - Practice computers (1:1 ratio)  - Operating system control panel/settings documentation  - Sample policy templates
assessments: Knowledge   - Outcome of peer review  Skills   - Observation of practical skill in configuration  - Verification of configured account restrictions

schedule.sessionTitle: Importance and Types of Data Backup
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain the critical importance of computer software backup.  b. Describe different types of computer software backup strategies.  c. Choose a suitable backup type based on given recovery point and time objectives.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Initiate a discussion on the risks of data loss and the necessity of backup.  - Deliver a presentation differentiating between full, incremental, and differential backups.  - Conduct a case study analysis where trainees propose backup solutions for various scenarios.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Contribute to the discussion, sharing experiences and understanding of data loss risks.  - Engage with the presentation, identifying key differences between backup types.  - Collaborate on the case study, proposing and justifying chosen backup types for each scenario.  Assignment: Outline a backup strategy for a small business's critical data, specifying backup types and frequency.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Iheagwara & Blyth (2003) – best practices in deployment planning & backup strategies  Resources;   - Articles on data loss prevention  - Backup software documentation  - PowerPoint presentation  - Whiteboard
assessments: Attitude  - Active participation in discussion  Skills   - Accuracy in differentiating backup types  Knowledge   - Quality of proposed backup solutions

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Plan the steps for creating a data backup using backup software.  b. Execute the process of creating a full and an incremental backup.  c. Perform a basic data restoration from a created backup.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Demonstrate the use of a backup utility to create different types of backups.  - Guide trainees through a hands-on exercise to create their own backups of specified data.  - Instruct trainees on the procedure to restore data from a previously created backup.
traineeActivities: Trainee to:   - Observe the demonstration of backup creation and data restoration processes.  - Practice creating full and incremental backups of sample data on their computers.  - Perform a data restoration exercise, verifying the integrity of the restored files.  Assignment: Document the entire backup and restore procedure for a personal computer, including screenshots.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Iheagwara & Blyth (2003) – best practices in deployment planning & backup strategies  Resources;   - Backup software (e.g., Windows Backup, third-party tools)  - External storage devices (flash drives, external HDDs)  - Practice computers (1:1 ratio)  - Installation manuals
assessments: Skills  - Practical demonstration of backup/restore skills  - Verification of backup integrity  Knowledge   - Review of documented procedure

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify various computer software installation media.  b. Differentiate between common computer software installation methods.  c. Select the appropriate installation media and method based on software type and environment.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Present and discuss different forms of software installation media (e.g., optical discs, USB, network shares, cloud).  - Organize a matching exercise to link installation methods (e.g., silent, custom, unattended) with scenarios.  - Facilitate a group discussion on choosing the optimal installation approach for specific software deployments.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Engage with the presentation, examining and discussing different installation media types.  - Participate in the matching exercise, correctly associating methods with scenarios.  - Contribute to the group discussion, articulating justifications for chosen installation media and methods.  Assignment: Research and describe the typical installation media and methods for a popular operating system and a specific enterprise application.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Microsoft (2021) – official guide for Windows installation media creation  Resources;   - Sample installation CDs/DVDs and USB drives  - Documentation on network installation services  - PowerPoint presentation  - Internet access
assessments: Skills   - Performance in matching exercise  - Quality of group discussion contributions  Knowledge  - Accuracy of researched descriptions

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Describe various types of software registration and licensing.  b. Perform the general steps required to install computer software.  c. Confirm the successful installation and basic functionality of installed software.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Explain different software licensing models (e.g., perpetual, subscription, open-source) and registration processes.  - Demonstrate the end-to-end installation of a common application, including registration prompts.  - Supervise trainees as they install a given software package, providing assistance as needed.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Listen to the explanation and discuss licensing models, asking questions for clarity.  - Observe the demonstration of software installation, paying attention to registration steps.  - Install a specified software package on their computers and verify its functionality.  Assignment: Install a free or trial software application, document the installation process, and note any registration steps.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Microsoft (2021) – official guide for Windows installation media creation  Resources;   - Software installation manuals  - Software licensing agreements samples  - Computers (1:1 ratio) with installer files  - Projector
assessments: Skills   - Observation of installation process  - Verification of installed software functionality  Knowledge   - Review of documented installation steps

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Research and identify suitable anti-malware solutions for different user needs.  b. Compare features and capabilities of various anti-malware software.  c. Select appropriate anti-malware acquisition methods based on budget and requirements.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Lead a guided research session for trainees to explore anti-malware products and their features.  - Facilitate a comparative analysis activity, highlighting pros and cons of different solutions.  - Discuss various acquisition methods for anti-malware software (e.g., free, subscription, bundled).
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Conduct guided research on anti-malware solutions, gathering information on features and reviews.  - Engage in the comparative analysis, evaluating anti-malware products based on specific criteria.  - Participate in the discussion on acquisition methods, outlining suitable options for different scenarios.  Assignment: Select an anti-malware solution for a home user and justify your choice based on its features and acquisition cost.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Russinovich et al. (2017) Ch.2 – covers Windows installation types, performance impact, and optimization  Resources;   - Internet access for research  - Cybersecurity blogs and reviews  - Product datasheets of anti-malware software  - Computers (1:1 ratio)
assessments: Knowledge   - Quality of research findings  Skills   - Critical thinking in comparative analysis  - Justification in assignment

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Prepare a system for anti-malware software installation.  b. Execute the installation process for a chosen anti-malware solution.  c. Verify the successful installation and initial operational status of the anti-malware software.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Demonstrate the best practices for preparing a system (e.g., removing existing antivirus) before installing new anti-malware.  - Guide trainees through a practical session to install an anti-malware application on a test machine.  - Instruct trainees on how to check the anti-malware's status and perform initial virus definition updates.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Observe the demonstration of system preparation and take notes on essential pre-installation steps.  - Perform the installation of an anti-malware application on their designated test computers.  - Verify the installation status and initiate virus definition updates, troubleshooting any encountered issues.  Assignment: Install a free anti-malware program on a virtual machine and document the installation and initial setup steps.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  SANS Institute (2021) – security best practices for endpoint protection & patch management  Resources;   - Anti-malware installer files  - Test computers/virtual machines (1:1 ratio)  - Installation manuals/guides  - Internet connection for updates
assessments: Skills   - Observation of installation procedure  Knowledge   - Verification of anti-malware operational status  - Review of documented installation steps

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify key configuration settings within anti-malware software.  b. Adjust anti-malware settings to meet specific security policies.  c. Schedule and initiate system scans and definition updates.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Demonstrate the configuration options within various anti-malware interfaces.  - Present different security scenarios and task trainees to configure anti-malware accordingly.  - Guide trainees in setting up automated scan schedules and definition update frequencies.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Observe the demonstration of anti-malware configuration, noting important settings.  - Apply configurations to anti-malware software on their test machines based on given scenarios.  - Configure and test automated scan and update schedules, verifying their functionality.  Assignment: Customize the scan settings of an installed anti-malware to perform a deep scan weekly and a quick scan daily.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  SANS Institute (2021) – security best practices for endpoint protection & patch management  Resources;   - Anti-malware software installed on practice machines  - Security policy templates  - User manuals for anti-malware software
assessments: Skills   - Practical demonstration of configuration skills  - Verification of scheduled tasks  - Assessment of customized settings

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain the significance of proper software configuration for performance and security.  b. Justify configuration decisions based on user requirements and system environment.  c. Identify potential issues arising from misconfigured software.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Lead a discussion on the impact of configuration on software efficiency and security.  - Present case studies of misconfigured software leading to vulnerabilities or performance degradation.  - Facilitate a problem-solving session where trainees propose optimal configurations for hypothetical systems.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Contribute to the discussion, sharing insights on the importance of configuration.  - Analyze the presented case studies, identifying the causes and effects of misconfigurations.  - Collaborate in problem-solving, proposing and defending their optimal software configurations.  Assignment: Write a short report detailing three real-world examples of how misconfigured software led to significant problems.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Kaner et al. (1999) Ch.10 – software deployment strategies & verification methods  Resources;   - Articles on software security and optimization  - Case studies of system failures  - Whiteboard and markers
assessments: Knowledge   - Active participation in discussions  Skills   - Analytical skills in case study discussions  - Quality of written report

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify various tools available for computer software configuration.  b. Demonstrate the basic use of selected software configuration tools.  c. Select the appropriate configuration tool for different software types and tasks.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Introduce different types of configuration tools (e.g., GUI-based, command-line, scripting).  - Demonstrate practical use of a system's built-in configuration tools (e.g., 'msconfig', 'regedit').  - Guide trainees through exercises using these tools to modify software settings.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Observe the introduction to configuration tools and discuss their applications.  - Practice using the demonstrated configuration tools to adjust software settings.  - Select and apply the appropriate tool for given configuration tasks, justifying their choice.  Assignment: Explore and document the functions of 'Task Manager' and 'System Information' utilities for software configuration and monitoring.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  National Institute of Standards and Technology (2020) – digital identity & authentication guidelines (applied to local account policies)  Resources;   - Computers (1:1 ratio)  - Operating system utilities documentation  - Online tutorials for specific configuration tools
assessments: Skills   - Observation of practical use of tools  - Accuracy of configuration modifications  - Quality of documentation

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Troubleshoot common software installation errors and failures.  b. Apply best practices for efficient and secure software installation.  c. Optimize software installations for specific performance or security requirements.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Present common installation error messages and guide trainees through troubleshooting steps.  - Lead a workshop on best practices like clean installs, dependency management, and silent installations.  - Provide scenarios where trainees must plan and execute an optimized software installation.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Analyze common installation errors and participate in troubleshooting exercises.  - Practice applying installation best practices during simulated software deployments.  - Develop and execute optimized installation plans for given scenarios.  Assignment: Research a complex software application and outline its recommended installation best practices, including any pre-requisites.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Nielsen & Loranger (2006) Ch.3 – usability principles for software configuration & user interface customization  Resources;   - Software troubleshooting guides  - Online forums and knowledge bases  - Virtual machines for practice  - Installation manuals
assessments: Skills   - Problem-solving during troubleshooting  - Evaluation of optimized installation plans  Attitude   - Observation of applied best practices

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Customize software settings for advanced user preferences and system integration.  b. Automate software configurations using scripting or deployment tools.  c. Document complex software configurations for future reference and reproducibility.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Demonstrate advanced configuration adjustments, such as registry edits or group policy modifications (with caution).  - Introduce basic scripting for automated configuration and provide templates.  - Guide trainees in developing comprehensive documentation for their complex configurations.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Observe the demonstration of advanced configuration techniques, understanding potential impacts.  - Practice using scripting or configuration tools to automate basic software settings.  - Create detailed documentation for a configured software, including steps and justification.  Assignment: Write a simple script to automate the configuration of a specified software's startup behavior.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Seacord (2003) Ch.6 – configuration management & change control in software maintenance  Resources;   - Operating system registry editor and group policy editor  - Scripting language documentation (e.g., PowerShell, Bash)  - Configuration management tools
assessments: Skills   - Practical application of advanced techniques  - Functionality of automated scripts  - Clarity and completeness of documentation

Recall knowledge of local user account management procedures.  c. Explain concepts related to data backup and general software installation principles.

trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Administer the practical continuous assessment test, providing clear instructions.  - Observe trainees' performance during the practical tasks, ensuring compliance.  - Evaluate the outcomes of the practical tasks against defined criteria.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain the fundamental importance of software testing in the software lifecycle.  b. Describe various computer software testing techniques.  c. Categorize testing techniques based on their application and objectives.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Deliver an introductory presentation on why software testing is crucial and its benefits.  - Present different testing techniques (e.g., unit, integration, system, acceptance testing).  - Lead a mind-mapping activity to help trainees categorize and understand testing techniques.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;   - Participate in the presentation by discussing the importance of quality assurance.  - Engage with the presentation, identifying and discussing various testing techniques.  - Collaborate in the mind-mapping activity, classifying testing techniques based on their characteristics.  Assignment: Research and write a short report on the consequences of inadequate software testing in a well-known software failure.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify common software testing tools like Test Complete and Selenium.  b. Explain the primary functionalities and use cases of these tools.  c. Differentiate between Test Complete and Selenium based on their features and application areas.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Introduce Test Complete and Selenium, highlighting their history and main features.  - Demonstrate basic test case creation and execution using simplified versions or simulations of these tools.  - Lead a comparative discussion, emphasizing the strengths and weaknesses of each tool.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Recognize mobile and API testing tools such as Appium and Postman.  b. Describe the specific applications and benefits of Appium for mobile testing.  c. Understand how Postman is utilized for API testing and development.

assessments: Skills   - Practical exercise completion with Postman  - Engagement in discussion  - Review of documented API test

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Prepare basic test cases based on software requirements.  b. Execute fundamental functional tests on a software application.  c. Document test results and identify basic defects.

resourcesAndRefs: References;  Iheagwara & Blyth (2003) – usability evaluation methods in deployed software systems  Resources;   - Sample software application for testing  - Test case templates  - Defect tracking forms  - Computers (1:1 ratio)
assessments: Skills   - Quality of test cases  - Observation of test execution  - Accuracy of defect documentation

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Conduct integration tests between multiple software components.  b. Analyze software performance and identify potential bottlenecks.  c. Report comprehensive testing findings and recommendations.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;   - Demonstrate the process of setting up and executing integration tests for two connected applications.  - Introduce basic performance testing concepts and tools, guiding trainees in analyzing system behavior.  - Lead a workshop on creating detailed test reports, including executive summaries and technical details.
traineeActivities: Trainee to;  - Observe the demonstration of integration testing setup and execution.  - Participate in exercises to analyze basic software performance metrics.  - Prepare and present a comprehensive test report based on simulated testing activities.  Assignment: Research common performance bottlenecks in software and suggest three mitigation strategies.
resourcesAndRefs: References;  Microsoft (2021) – error handling guidelines in Windows applications (applied generically)  Resources;   - Integrated software applications for testing  - Basic performance monitoring tools (e.g., Task Manager, Resource Monitor)  - Test report templates
assessments: Skills   - Observation of integration testing skills  - Analytical skills in performance analysis  - Quality of test report presentation

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Classify different types of corrective measures for software defects.  b. Explain the application of various corrective measures in different scenarios.  c. Identify the triggers and impact of implementing specific corrective actions.
trainerActivities: Trainer to;  - Present a taxonomy of corrective measures (e.g., hotfixes, patches, major revisions).  - Lead a discussion on when and why each type of corrective measure would be applied.  - Facilitate a problem-solution matching activity for different software defect types.
